answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent network can anchor identities to radio multipath channel sounding. A node verifies presence by digitizing pulse reflections scattered off a riparian willow stand, a sheer raven cliff, and a stone relic. An adversary must operate discrete physical transceivers at distinct geographic sites per identity, bearing hardware fabrication and property deployment costs. However, wind-swayed foliage alters echo profiles, occasionally causing false rejections.
